sentences.text: Senior Civil Judge & MACT, Srirangapatna have preferred this appeal.
3. Claimant No.1 is the wife, claimant Nos.2 to 9 are the sons and daughters and claimant No.10 is the mother of deceased Shivanappa Vaddar.

On 01.08.2017 at 7.00 p.m. when Shivanappa Vaddar was proceeding near the land of one Swamynayaka within the limits of Rangasamudra village,
Mysuru District, the Motor vehicle bearing No.KA 55-L -3459 hit him.
Consequently he suffered grievous injuries.
Initially he was treated in Government Hospital, Bannur.
From there he was shifted to Mission Hospital, Mysore.
On 04.08.2017 he succumbed to the injuries in Mission Hospital.
4. At the relevant time, respondent Nos.1 and 2 were the registered owner and Insurer of the said motor vehicle.

The appellants filed MVC No.1271/2017 before the Tribunal against the respondents claiming compensation of Rs.32,20,000/- on the ground that they were all dependent on income of the deceased and due to his death they have suffered damages under several heads.

5. Respondent Nos.1 and 2 contested the petition denying the rashness and negligence on the part of the rider of the motor cycle, age occupation, income of the deceased and their liability to pay the compensation.

The Tribunal on recording the evidence and hearing the parties by the impugned award held that the accident and the consequent death occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-55 L 3459.

The Tribunal considered the income of the deceased at Rs.7,000/- per month and his age at 44 years, deducted one-fourth out of the said income for his personal expenses, added 25% by way of future prospects applied 14 multiplier and awarded the compensation of Rs.11,02,584/- under the head loss of dependency.
6. The Tribunal considering the other heads in all awarded Rs.12,40,189/- as per the table below.

7. Learned counsel for the appellant reiterating the grounds of appeal submits that the Tribunal should have deducted one-fifth for the personal expenses.
He further submits that the income considered by the Tribunal is on the lower side and the compensation awarded on the other heads is also on the lower side.
Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.2 justified the impugned award.
8. Appellant Nos.2 and 5 are the major sons and appellant Nos.3, 4 and 6 are married daughters.
Therefore, the Tribunal was justified in holding that they were not the dependents of the deceased.
Though it is contended that they were also depending upon him, they were not examined before the Tribunal to say that they were depending on the deceased.
Therefore, only appellant Nos.1 and 7 to 10 have to be treated as dependents.
9. The occurrence of the accident due to rash and negligent driving of the motor cycle is not in dispute.
The insured has not challenged the findings with regard to the age of the deceased.
Of course, there was no proof to show that the deceased was earning Rs.20,000/- per month as contended by the claimants.
Therefore, the income was to be assessed notionally.
The accident occurred on 01.08.2017.
The deceased was working as mason.
Having regard to the nature of the work and the prevalent cost of living and inflation the Tribunal should have considered his income at Rs.11,000/- per month.

10. As per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in National Insurance Company Limited vs.
Pranay Sethi1 and having regard to the age and employment, 25% has to be super added to the income towards future prospects which AIR 2017 SC 5157 comes to Rs.11000 + 2750=13750/-.

sentences.text: As per the judgment in Sarla Varma v. Delhi Transport Corporation2 one-fourth of the income has to be deducted for his personal expenses.

sentences.text:
Therefore, three-fourths of his income has to be considered for payment of compensation on the head of loss of dependency which comes to Rs.13750X  X12 X 14= 17,32,584/-.
11.
On the conventional heads of funeral expenses and loss of estate as per the judgment in Pranay Sethi's case Rs.15,000/- each with escalation of 10% has to be awarded which comes to Rs.33,000/-.
The compensation of Rs.27,605/- awarded under the head of medical expenses was based on records and calls for no interference.

Since the victim was hospitalized for 4 days, attendant charges,
food and nourishment Rs.300/- per day has to be awarded which comes to Rs.1,200/-.
So far as the consortium, 10 persons are shown as dependents and out of them appellant Nos.2 to 6 are major sons and married daughters.
It would not be reasonable to saddle the insurer with the burden of paying consortium to them.
Appellant Nos.1, 7 to 10 have to be awarded AIR 2009 SC 3104 compensation under the head consortium.
As per the judgment in Pranay Sethi's case each of them are entitled to compensation of Rs.40,000/- with the escalation of 10% which comes to Rs.2,20,000/-.

Therefore, the just compensation payable is as follows:

sentences.text: The Tribunal held that appellant No.1 and 7 to 10 being the widow, aged mother and unmarried daughters and son aged 18 years alone are entitled to compensation.
That finding warrants no interference.
The appeal deserves to be partly allowed.

Hence the following:
ORDER i) The appeal is partly allowed.
ii) The impugned judgment and award dated 29.06.2019 is modified as follows:
a) Appellant/Claimant Nos.1, 7 to 10 are entitled to compensation of Rs.20,14,389/-
with interest thereon at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
b) Respondent No.2 Insurer shall deposit the said amount before the Tribunal after adjusting the amount already deposited if any, within six weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this order.
c) The order of the Tribunal with regard to apportionment and investment is maintained.
